title: Construction of a crystalline 14-metal Zn–Nd rectangular nanocluster with a dual-emissive response towards metal ions

material_class.structural_family: centrosymmetric rectangular Zn6Nd8 nanocluster with two flexible Schiff-base ligands

synthesis.procedure: Zn(OAc)2·2H2O (0.30 mmol, 0.0666 g), Nd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.40 mmol, 0.1800 g) and H2L (0.10 mmol, 0.0417 g) were dissolved in 10 mL EtOH, 2 mL MeOH and 2 mL DMF at room temperature, then a solution of triethylamine in EtOH (0.01 mol L−1, 2 mL) was added. The resulting solution was heated under reflux for 30 min and filtered at room temperature. Pale yellow crystals of 1 were obtained by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate at room temperature after three weeks. The product was collected and dried in an oven at 120 °C for two hours. Reactions were performed under dry oxygen-free dinitrogen using standard Schlenk techniques.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature dissolution and crystallization; reflux during reaction; oven drying at 120 °C
synthesis.time: reflux 30 min; crystallization three weeks; drying two hours
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk techniques under dry N2; reflux then diethyl-ether diffusion crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered at room temperature; yellow crystals grown by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate; collected and dried at 120 °C

properties.summary: Cluster 1 is dual-emissive: ligand-centered visible emission at 494 nm and typical Nd3+ NIR emission (most intense 4F3/2 → 4I11/2 line at 1061 nm) upon 355 nm excitation in MeCN and the solid state. Intrinsic Nd quantum yield 2.2% from τ/τ0, overall NIR quantum yield 0.7%, ligand-to-Nd sensitization efficiency 31.8%. In DMF it shows dual fluorescent sensing of metal ions, with highest sensitivity to K+ and Co2+ at the ppm level (NIR quenching and visible enhancement/quenching).
